description: Exploit AVX-512 VBMI2's VPCOMPRESSB/VPEXPANDB instructions to implement zero-copy token extraction. Instead of copying matched tokens to a separate buffer, use VPCOMPRESSB with a mask to densely pack only structural characters or only string content directly from the input register, enabling branchless extraction of variable-length fields without memory allocation or data movement.
mathematical_formalization: Given input register R[0..63] and mask M identifying relevant bytes, VPCOMPRESSB(R, M) produces R'[0..popcount(M)-1] in a single instruction. Traditional extraction: O(popcount(M)) scalar stores. VPCOMPRESSB: O(1) instruction, O(popcount(M)/64) stores. Speedup ~ 64 for sparse structural characters.
analogical_connections: Column-store compression (BitWeaving): bit-parallel operations on compressed data in-place
FPGA stream processing: hardware-level compress/expand native to stream architectures
SingleStore VBMI2 usage: demonstrated compress/expand for high-throughput byte shuffling in database operations
implementation_hypothesis: In structural indexing, after identifying structural characters via SIMD comparison, use VPCOMPRESSB to extract only structural bytes into a dense buffer. For string extraction during on-demand parsing, use VPCOMPRESSB with inverted mask to pack string content. For Unicode escape handling, use VPEXPANDB to scatter decoded codepoints.
experiment_seed: Implement token extraction microbenchmarks comparing scalar loop, VPCOMPRESSB-based, and PSHUFB-based extraction. Measure on Ice Lake / Sapphire Rapids with varying token densities (1%, 5%, 25%).
